meta.analysis: A single detection rule cannot correlate a DNS resolution of a redirector (Phase 1) with an anomalous programmatic sign-in (Phase 2) hours later. This phased hunt uses an agent to link user behavior across disparate surfaces.

stages.name: Session Replay via Residential Proxy

scenario.summary: This campaign leverages a deceptive Microsoft Teams booking workflow to facilitate device code phishing. Attackers lead victims through a multi-stage redirect chain to a typosquatted domain hosting an encrypted phishing kit that initiates a Microsoft device code sign-in, ultimately capturing OAuth tokens and session cookies for account takeovers via residential proxies.

meta.rationale: Scope to hosts with Microsoft Teams installed. Focus on users in executive or finance roles who are more likely to be targeted by such a sophisticated spear-phishing lure.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker is using a multi-stage redirect chain and a convincing Microsoft Teams booking lure to trick users into authorizing a device code, subsequently replaying the stolen session tokens via residential proxies using programmatic tools.

hunt.name: Microsoft Teams Booking Device Code Phishing
hunt.description: This hunt follows the lifecycle of a device code phishing attack identified in recent research. It identifies users who interacted with a typosquatted Teams booking site through a redirect chain involving Google short links and then correlates that web interaction with subsequent anomalous identity events. The follow-on phase looks for the specific 'Cmsi:Cmsi' login flow and session abuse by programmatic user agents (Python, Node) replaying tokens through residential proxies. An agent correlates these two surfaces to confirm successful compromise.

nodes.label: Prevalence of programmatic user agents in sign-ins

config.content: SELECT LOWER(user_agent) AS ua, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS users, COUNT(*) AS signins, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider IN ('m365', 'azure_ad') AND (instr(',' || '{{programmatic_uas}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(user_agent) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(user_agent) LIKE 'python%' OR LOWER(user_agent) LIKE 'node%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY LOWER(user_agent) HAVING users <= 3 ORDER BY users ASC
config.description: Stack-count user agents to identify rare programmatic sign-ins (Python, Node) that stand out from standard browser traffic.
config.expected_signal: A programmatic user agent seen for only a few users, suggesting attacker automation replaying session tokens. Standard browser traffic should be common across the fleet.
